Question B-003-003-010.

Why the correct answer is right: In this block-level frequency modulation (FM) receiver view, squelch mutes or enables recovered audio, so it is associated with the audio-frequency (AF) amplifier/audio section.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Limiter": The limiter prepares a constant-amplitude intermediate-frequency (IF) signal for the discriminator, not the user mute gate for quiet audio.
- sourceIndex 2: "IF amplifier": The IF amplifier supplies gain before detection. Squelch acts on whether audio is heard.
- sourceIndex 3: "Product detector": A product detector recovers single-sideband (SSB) and continuous-wave (CW) signals; it is not the FM receiver squelch block.
